messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Paging maya (oncall) — p99 latency SLO breach detected for canary service 'text-gen-canary' in us-west-2. Current alert: p99 = 2.8s (SLO 1.5s). Traffic shift at 5367890000 by deploy-id: rfd-2026-03-canary.
maya: on it — 1st looking at dashboards, will grab traces. anyone see correlated errors? :eyes:
samir: I see a sharp p99 bump starting ~5367890010 coincident with the traffic shift. p95 is up but not as bad. streaming stalls show a spike in websocket reconnects.
jin: deploy-bot reported 20% of production traffic routed to canary at 5367890000. Canary model = v13-encoder-quant. Recent runtime change: small KV cache policy tweak pushed yesterday.
deploy-bot: deploy rfd-2026-03-canary started by anjali at 5367889980. rollout step: traffic 0->20% at 5367890000. No automated rollback triggered.
maya: ok, mounting flamegraphs now. samir — can you check per-node tail latency? suspect single host hot path.
samir: grabbing node-level histo. quick psuedo-query:
```
avg(p99_latency) by host where service="text-gen-canary" and region="us-west-2"
```
results: host-12 p99=7.2s, host-8 p99=2.1s, others ~0.9-1.2s. host-12 is the outlier.
elaine: support seeing elevated error reports for streaming sessions dropping after ~1-2s. A couple of enterprise customers reported truncated responses.
ops-bot: noticed KV cache warmup failures on host-12 — evictions skyrocketed during rollout. logs show repeated kv-miss + recompute for long sequences.
jin: that maps — v13-encoder-quant increases KV footprint slightly; combined with cache policy tweak may cause thrash on smaller hosts.
maya: agree. mitigation options: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% (stop rollout), 2) pin canary to fewer hosts excluding host-12, 3) roll back to previous model version (v12). Priority: minimize customer impact.
samir: quick impact numbers: 1.1% of overall requests were on canary, but because of tail at host-12 it's responsible for ~18% of p99 errors we surface to customers.
maya: @deploy-bot — can you cut traffic back to 0% for rollout rfd-2026-03-canary? we want an immediate stop.
deploy-bot: Ack. Running traffic cut command:
```
redwood deploy traffic --id rfd-2026-03-canary --set 0%
```
Executing…

Status: SUCCESS — traffic set to 0% at 5367890146. No new canary requests will be routed.
maya: good. let's watch p99 in next 30s.
jin: also adding a temporary host drain for host-12 to remove hot node from serving pool.
ops-bot: draining host-12 — connections migrating. drain command:
```
kubectl annotate node host-12 redwood/drain=true && redwood node drain host-12 --grace 10s
```
samir: after traffic cut and drain, p99 across region down to 1.0s within two minutes. streaming reconnects reduced by ~85%.
elaine: support: customer reports also dropping quickly. notifying affected accounts: acct-88 and acct-102 — minimal data loss, sending incident message.
maya: patch triage: root likely interaction between kv-cache policy change + model v13's larger KV working set. Action items: rollback canary model in CI and revisit cache policy.
samir: for rollback we can do two things: 1) full rollback to v12, or 2) re-run canary with lower concurrency and explicit KV warmup. Recommend rollback to v12 for now.
maya: agree — prioritize safety. @deploy-bot please rollback model to v12 for canary group and block re-rollouts until follow-up.
deploy-bot: Rollback command:
```
redwood deploy model --target canary --from v12 --force --note "incident rollback"
```
Executing rollback…

Status: ROLLBACK STARTED at 5367890198. Estimated completion ~30s.

Deploy logs: step 1/3 pull v12 image, step 2/3 reload model on hosts, step 3/3 health checks.

Health check warnings on host-9 for GPU allocation but passing.

Rollback COMPLETED at 5367890235. Canary now running v12.
maya: monitoring — p99 stable at 0.95s, streaming stalls resolved. moving to inform SRE and Customer Success.
jin: logging root cause hypothesis in incident tracker: "kv-cache policy + v13 KV working set => host-level thrash". Adding traces and host metrics to ticket.
elaine: I've messaged affected customers with summary and remediation steps. no billing adjustments required yet, but CS ops will follow up.
ops-bot: capturing logs and core dumps from host-12 for postmortem. archiving to s3://redwood-incident-archives/5367890123/
samir: follow-ups: 1) rollback gating: require KV warmup test for quant models, 2) revert cache policy tweak or make it adaptive, 3) run load test with v13 on staging with KV-heavy prompts.
maya: assigning follow-ups — samir (cache + staging tests), jin (deploy gating + CI checks), anjali (owner of rollout) will schedule postmortem. oncall clear for now. handing back to ops for cleanup.
maya: final status — mitigated. incident severity: Sev2 (customer impact limited, mitigated via traffic cut + rollback). Will file postmortem and notify leadership.
samir: noting timeline in ticket: detect 5367890010, traffic cut 5367890146, rollback complete 5367890235, mitigation verified 5367890245.
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged/closed by maya at 5367890250. :white_check_mark:"
